## Hands-on 4 – Exploring the menu {#hands-on-4-exploring-the-menu .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 4 is exploratory.** Try several specifications, look at what each one does, and get a feel for which decisions move the estimate.

1. Start from the reference: `try_spec()`
2. Change **one decision**, for example `try_spec(cohorts = "five_years")`, and read the estimate, its ratio, its test and its place among the `r nrow(curve)`; `my_experiments()` lists every try
3. Do it again with a different decision. Three or four is plenty, and ask for one option that is off the curve, such as `try_spec(histories = "score_file")`, to read why it is refused
4. Rerun the one that you can argue for best, so that it is your last try, and **submit it** with `submit_exploration()`
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Your result appears on the live **Multiverse** page within seconds, as an open circle.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
This is **not** your preregistered analysis. You are allowed to look, change your mind and try again, which is why this phase has a name of its own.
:::

::: notes
Task 4 is exploration. Start from the reference with try underscore spec and no arguments, which gives minus nought point seven three. Then change one decision and read what happens to the estimate, its ratio, its test and its place among the hundred and forty-four. The cohort window is a good first move, because it moves the estimate more than any other decision on the curve. Every try is logged, and my underscore experiments lists them side by side. Do it again with a different decision; three or four goes is plenty. Ask for the file of the analysts as well, and read the reason that comes back with the refusal. Then rerun the one you can argue for best and send it with submit underscore exploration. [advance] It appears on the Multiverse page within seconds. [advance] And this is not your preregistered analysis.
:::
